
### multiple APs, one network 


![](/multiaccess/cnsp-fig48.svg){width=1000px}

[Computer Networks: A Systems Approach, figure 48]{.mycredit}

### APs as switches  {.smaller}


* multiple APs can act as <i>one network</i>
* example: nodes connected to different APs can send packets to each other by MAC address 
<hr class="vspace" />
* distribution system needs to share neighbor-table-like information


### switching APs  {.smaller}


* nodes can switch APs… 
<hr class="vspace" />
* check for new APs when signal strength too low
* periodically check for beacons + signal strength 
<hr class="vspace" />
* switching APs = same as joining network, but…  

   * can keep IP address, etc.
   * maybe optimizations to avoid redoing wifi security, etc.



### cellular networks 


* for wifi networks, feasible to track device locations centrally mostly 
<hr class="vspace" />
* need/have something more complex for cellular networks


### cellular network model 


* cellular networks: base stations don't have full routing info
* instead: base stations identify gateway each end-host uses
* connections to gateways configured centrally


### a confusing picture 


![](/multiaccess/sysapp-fig53){}


### cellular mobility model (1)  {.smaller}

<table>
<tr><td>cell phone</td><td>$\rightarrow$</td><td>base station</td><td>$\rightarrow$</td><td>service gateway</td><td>$\rightarrow$</td><td>PDN gateway</td></tr>
<tr><td>(UE)</td><td></td><td>(BBU)</td><td></td><td>(SGW)</td><td></td><td>(PGW)</td></tr>
<tr><td></td></tr>
</table>
 

* central ‘mobility management entity’ (MME) sets up ‘tunnels’ for steps above 

   * coordinates with home subscriber server (HSS)
   * base stations don't track full routing information

* PDN gateway stays stable so IP address can stay the same 

   * PDN gateway = gateway to actual Internet



### cellular mobility model (2)  {.smaller}

<table>
<tr><td>cell phone</td><td>$\rightarrow$</td><td>base station</td><td>$\rightarrow$</td><td>service gateway</td><td>$\rightarrow$</td><td>PDN gateway</td></tr>
<tr><td>(UE)</td><td></td><td>(BBU)</td><td></td><td>(SGW)</td><td></td><td>(PGW)</td></tr>
<tr><td></td></tr>
</table>
 
<hr class="vspace" /> 

* if ‘roaming’:
* service gateway run by network you're connected to
* PDN gateway run by ‘home’ network
